| [CLAIM-454](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-454.md) | A latent feature or mode recovered from an organization's members' activity is at most a constituent of an organizational perspective, not the perspective: a feature allocation says which members take part in which modes, and whether those modes are organized into one perspective depends on the relations of access, uptake and authority among their carriers, which the same allocation leaves open | From the Northstar turns of the exchange "Experimental Infrastructure Review", where the owner proposed inferring an organization's perspectives with hLDA (T21) and the Indian buffet process (T22). Every reply made the same reservation, and T22 put it most plainly: "None of those ingredients alone is the perspective. The organized relationship among them is." It is the criterion [QUESTION-276](../../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-276.md)'s answer has to meet. It does not say features are useless, or that no perspective is ever one feature's carriers. It says the allocation underdetermines the perspective. | Proposed |
| [CLAIM-457](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-457.md) | That no single institution can bring about a remedy does not imply that no combination of them can: the institutions able together to realize a corrective outcome need include none able alone, so a true statement of unilateral inability is not a statement that the outcome is unattainable | A8 and A9 of the exchange of 2026-10-26, on the owner's CECOT case at U7: the United States said it could not bring a man back from Salvadoran custody, and El Salvador's president that he could not send him. Both can be true while the two together can, and the June 2025 return showed they could. Demonstrated by a construction. | [CLAIM-490](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-490.md) | A fanbase is a mixture of spectators who relate to the club in different ways, as supporters, followers, fans and flâneurs, so the public stance credited to it is weighted towards the most committed types before any bias in who is sampled | From Giulianotti's taxonomy ([THEORY-1111](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1111.md)): supporters are hot and bound to the club as community, while flâneurs are cool consumers who switch clubs. The expressions that make up "the fans hate the owner" come from the hot types, and the cool ones take no part. So the stance is the committed segment's by composition, before amplification or preference falsification. It does not say the committed segment is a minority, or that its stance is illegitimate. | Proposed |
| [CLAIM-493](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-493.md) | When a fanbase is set against an outside party such as its club's owner, its more extreme members become more prototypical of it, so a vocal minority can fix the fanbase's public stance through a group process and not only through biased sampling of who speaks | A derivation from self-categorization theory: in an intergroup context the more extreme members of a group gain prototypicality (Turner et al. 1994, p. 458, reporting Haslam and Turner). If influence follows prototypicality (Turner 2005, unread), a fanbase opposed to its owner will treat its most hostile members as most representative. A minority stance can then become the fanbase's public stance by a group process that A2's preference falsification and amplification do not need. It does not say that the private majority agrees. | Proposed |
